keyIdeas: The Eco7 decision centers on launch pricing, distribution, and whether Aventage stores should receive exclusivity.
Eco7 is made with recycled oil, uses less production energy, and performs closer to a synthetic blend than to conventional oil.
DIFM consumers rely heavily on professional service providers; the installer recommendation is especially influential.
A full price of $6.75 supports premium positioning and stronger margins, while a $5.25 discounted price sells more easily but squeezes margins and may devalue the innovation.
Aventage exclusivity may improve store commitment, message consistency, and rollout execution, but narrower distribution limits reach.
Avellin planned to avoid national DIY retailers initially to gain support from DIFM installers and reduce channel conflict.
United's late outreach showed some recognition of the issue but came only after viral public pressure.
Offering compensation after public attention suggested willingness to revisit the grievance, but also made the response look reputation-driven.
Treating the incident as a training case acknowledged a systemic customer-service problem.
Not escalating legally was sensible because an aggressive response could have amplified backlash.
A better response would have resolved the complaint earlier, issued a timely public apology, and committed to concrete operational improvements.
